paper: Immervoll, Kleven, Kreiner & Saez (2007), 'Welfare Reform in European Countries: A Microsimulation Analysis', The Economic Journal 117(517):1-44

environment.gpu_model: NVIDIA RTX A6000 (x4, 49140 MiB each) - not needed; analysis is lightweight closed-form algebra

codebase_provenance: Shipped repo contained only EUROMOD.xls (20 sheets), cached CSV exports of each sheet, and one prep-check script (prep_checks/check_table2a.py). The table/figure driver scripts named in the plan did not exist and were written from scratch, re-implementing the paper's closed-form equations (15),(16),(18),(19) exactly as encoded in the shipped prep check.

step1_setup_and_prepcheck.detail: Installed xlrd/numpy/scipy/matplotlib. EUROMOD.xls opens; all expected sheets present (Read Me, Aggregate Run, Disaggregate Run, Tax-Benefit Data_1998, 15 country sheets AT/BE/DK/FI/FR/GE/GR/IR/IT/LU/NL/PT/SP/SW/UK, WeightsGermany). prep_checks/check_table2a.py prints 15 country rows, no missing-sheet/file errors.

step2_table2a_table7.match: EXACT to paper Table 2(a) and Table 7 cols (1)-(2) at 2 decimals for all 15 countries.

step3_table2b.match: EXACT to paper Table 2(b). All 15 countries: Dd==Dw to <1e-9 (True), tradeoff_demogrant <= tradeoff_workingpoor (True). e.g. AT 0.16/1.57 (demo) 0.16/2.16 (wp).

step4_table4.match: eps=0.1 block reproduces Table 2(a) exactly; eps=0 (panel a) and eps=0.2 (panel c) match paper Table 4. Paper's 'No Gainers'/'No Losers' degenerate cells (DK, and FI/SW/SP at eps=0.2) surface as NaN / negative-denominator trade-offs via the has_gainers flag.

step5_table6.match: Panel (a) reproduces Table 2(a). Panel (b) matches paper Table 6(b) closely (e.g. AT -0.29/2.31, -0.05/1.26; SW -0.42/4.30, -0.20/6.21; DK 'No Losers' -> NaN trade-off). DK demogrant trade-off 28.10 vs paper 29.09 (~3% gap; DK trade-off denominator is near-singular and hypersensitive).
step5_table6.note: The plan's expected-outcome claim that the working-poor trade-off stays BELOW the demogrant trade-off in every country in panel (b) is contradicted by the paper's own Table 6(b): Finland (4.65>4.10), Italy (1.84>1.82) and Sweden (6.21>4.30) have WP trade-off ABOVE demogrant, due to their very compressed earnings distributions. The reproduction faithfully matches the paper, not the plan's simplification.

step6_table3.match: ALL 45 values (15 countries x 3 critical elasticities) match paper Table 3 to 2 decimals. crit_identical<crit_zeroloss<crit_pareto holds for every country. Pareto condition implemented as 1-Dw = max_j(s_j/e_j) (richest worker just gains -> no losers -> Psi_w->0).

step7_figures.detail: figure1_marginal_tax_rates.pdf and figure2_participation_tax_rates.pdf, each 3 stacked panels (Nordic / Continental / Anglo-Saxon-Southern), deciles 1-10, one labelled line per country. tax_rates_by_decile.csv has 150 rows. Data read from 'Tax-Benefit Data_1998' sheet, 'Without Consumption Taxes' columns. Patterns match paper (Nordic high marginal rates; DK participation tax falls 77->60% across deciles).
step7_figures.caveat: Per plan: these tax rates are the shipped EUROMOD-computed inputs; EUROMOD cannot be re-run from restricted micro-data in this container, so figures plot the workbook's tax-rate data (as the plan specifies).

overall: All 7 steps reproduced. Tables 2a, 2b, 3, 4, 6 and Table 7 cols 1-2, plus Figures 1-2, all reproduce the paper's published values (Table 3: all 45 cells exact to 2dp; Tables 2a/2b exact; Table 6b within rounding except hypersensitive DK demogrant).
